$comment:
Urlencoded edition-to-lane case table, shared byte-for-byte by the three engines that build an
OpenAPI application/x-www-form-urlencoded request body: openbindings-go/formats/openapi,
openapi-client/go, and openapi-client/typescript/src (which openbindings-ts/packages/openapi
re-exports).

WHAT THIS TABLE GUARDS. Which of two lanes an urlencoded property takes when the artifact writes
no RFC6570-style control:

  style lane    RFC6570 form expansion of the property value (an object explodes into its own
                members), per the Encoding Object style/explode/allowReserved fields
  content lane  the property value encoded as one unit under the Encoding Object contentType,
                whose default for an object is application/json

The partition below is an EDITION partition, and it is not a matter of taste: 3.0.4 and the 3.1
line each state that an explicitly defined style, explode or allowReserved makes contentType
ignored -- which is only meaningful if contentType otherwise governs -- and 3.0.4 says outright
that with all three absent "Encoding is to be based on contentType alone". No 3.0.0-3.0.3 text
says anything of the kind, so on that line the Encoding Object style field applies with its
default, written or not.

DO NOT re-derive this partition from the sentence "the default serialization strategy of such
properties is described in the Encoding Object’s style property as form". That sentence is
present in 3.0.0, 3.0.1, 3.0.2, 3.0.3 AND 3.1.0, and absent from 3.0.4, 3.1.1 and 3.1.2
(reproduce: node corpus-lab/scripts/strip-oas-html.mjs --count "the default serialization
strategy of such properties is described in the Encoding Object.s style property as form"
-> 1/1/1/1/0/1/0/0). It does not partition the editions the way the lanes do, and an earlier
doc comment in all three engines cited it as though it did.

Each case is rendered as a WHOLE OpenAPI document and loaded through each Go engine’s own
loader, so the table exercises the shipped path rather than a hand-built typed model. Every
cell was observed in all three engines before it was written down; the authority quotations in
"basis" were verified against corpus-lab/authorities/texts/openapi/oas at the digests recorded
in corpus-lab/OPENAPI-RUNTIME.md.

Shape of every case: one urlencoded request body whose schema is
{type: object, properties: {address: {type: object, properties: {street: {type: string}}}}},
invoked with {"address": {"street": "main st"}}. An object-valued property is used because it is
the smallest value whose two lanes emit different bytes; a primitive emits the same bytes on
both lanes and would guard nothing.

cases.name: 3.0.0|no-encoding
cases.basis: No RFC6570-style control is written, so this cell IS the edition partition. No edition-3.0.0 rule lets contentType displace the RFC6570-style fields. The Encoding Object's style/explode/allowReserved descriptions (§4.7.15.1) say only that they SHALL be ignored when the body media type is not application/x-www-form-urlencoded, and §4.7.14.4 states that "the default serialization strategy of such properties is described in the Encoding Object’s style property as form". So style applies whether or not an Encoding Object is written.
